Yosef and Yehuda and the two Moshiachs
exile as division, redemption as unity

title.en: Why 'yimloch' and not 'melech'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Mechilta that had the Jews said 'Hashem melech' there would have been no more exile, and asks why they did not. He contrasts the twelve paths of the sea with the seven streams of the future and asks why the sea returned 'to its first condition' after the miracle.

title.en: Yosef and the redemption split in two

summary.en: Yosef's name alone points to the future redemption. The Mashgiach brings the Chida that 190 years of exile remained owed, so the redemption was split like Yachatz; the sea did not want to split before its time, but split for the merit of Yosef's coffin and his self-sacrifice beyond nature.

title.en: Song as a heavenly match of tones

summary.en: Before Shvi'i shel Pesach the Mashgiach discusses kinds of song: poetry whose lines rhyme, and niggun, tones that fit one another wondrously, unlike a cat walking on a piano. Like a shidduch, which only Hashem makes, this cannot be explained; he brings the Gra that most secrets of the Torah depend on the wisdom of music.

title.en: Seven tones and Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Tikkunei Zohar that a heavenly palace opens only through niggun, and explains that song has seven tones completed by Shabbos, the day of song. He tells of the Baal HaTanya answering the scholars of Shklov with a niggun, and links the seven tones to the seven days, the seven shepherds ending with David, the seven 'kol Hashem' of Havu laShem and the Beis HaMikdash harp.

title.en: Yaakov's niggun to unite Yosef and Yehuda

summary.en: Song at a wedding fits because a wedding is a match. The Mashgiach explains that Yaakov sent a niggun of Eretz Yisroel with 'mizimras ha'aretz' to awaken the union of Yosef and Yehuda, the two Moshiachs, whose rift born of jealousy, like the moon's, is the root of exile.

title.en: Noise without harmony; seven shepherds and twelve princes

summary.en: Tones with no connection to each other, like the music of the gentile world that Jews copy, arouse lowly desires, a union Hashem did not decree. The Mashgiach contrasts the seven shepherds, who belong to every Jew and unite in Shabbos, with the twelve tribal princes, each only for his own tribe, a state of separation.

title.en: Shabbos and Yerushalayim unite the tribes

summary.en: The twelve middle brachos of Shemoneh Esreh belong to the weekdays; on Shabbos one bracha gathers all Jews, like Yerushalayim, which was not divided among the tribes. The Mashgiach ties Shabbos, Yerushalayim, David and malchus together and explains that after the seven psalms of Kabbalas Shabbos one can sing.

title.en: White and black keys: chesed and din

summary.en: On the piano seven white keys bring out joy and five black half-keys bring out sadness, like shevarim. The Mashgiach explains white as chesed and black as din, and that joining them makes tiferes, the beauty of a niggun, and twelve tones. He brings the Mechilta reading 'bakosharos' as weeping and song.

title.en: Twelve tones of exile, seven of redemption

summary.en: Since Kerias Yam Suf was only half the redemption, it was still weeping with song, twelve tones like the twelve tribes before uniting under David. In the future there will be only the seven white tones of joy, the seven streams, gematria shirah; therefore at the sea they said 'yimloch', and in the future 'Hashem melech' will be said.

title.en: Shvi'i shel Pesach, the Shabbos of Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Likkutei Torah that Shvi'i shel Pesach is the Shabbos of Pesach, its greatest day, and the Sfas Emes that the open spaces of the Shirah show the heart opening. The haftorah is David's song, and Acharon shel Pesach's haftorah is of Moshiach; chassidim stressed saying the daily Shirah with joy.

title.en: Sefer Chareidim's easy segulos for atonement

summary.en: Like costly medicines next to free healing herbs in the field, Sefer Chareidim lists six easy segulos that bring atonement without fasts and hardship. The Mashgiach goes through five: answering Amen yehei shmei rabba with all one's strength, keeping Shabbos properly, letting slights pass, hisbodedus, and listening eagerly to a sage's words of aggadah.

title.en: The sixth segulah: the daily Shirah

summary.en: The sixth segulah is saying the Shirah daily with joy. The Mashgiach brings the Yalkut and the Zohar: one who says it daily with intent merits to say it in the future, Moshiach is found in it, and Knesses Yisroel is crowned with the crown prepared for Moshiach. Pesach is emunah, and the Shirah draws great miracles.

title.en: Daily miracles and the Jews of Eretz Yisroel

summary.en: The Jews of Eretz Yisroel, surrounded by enemies, need salvation beyond nature, and daily miracles go unnoticed. The Mashgiach brings the Ramban at the end of Bo and the Yaavetz that Jewish survival in exile is a greater miracle than the sea, and explains that the Shirah, which mentions the inhabitants of Peleshes, draws that salvation.

title.en: The real battle is in the beis medrash

summary.en: The war of Yishmael in Eretz Yisroel is a war against Hashem, as the attacks on the Jews of Meah Shearim show. The Mashgiach says the battle is fought in every shul and beis medrash, and every Jew is a soldier with Torah, tefillah and the daily Shirah said with joy.

title.en: Yom tov is redemption, not commemoration

summary.en: Jewish festivals are not commemorations of past events like a national holiday; every Pesach redemption comes down to the world, and each care with chametz nullifies the sitra achra. The Mashgiach closes with a brachah for salvation and for singing the new song of Moshiach.

catalogTitle: יום של התגלות עלמא דאתכסייא של כל יהודי אפילו של דתן ואבירם (ובענין גודל פגם המחלוקת)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that at the splitting of the sea the hidden world (alma d'iskasya) was revealed, so that even Dasan and Aviram, the worst of quarrelers, were awakened and had the sea split again for them, and that machlokes is the great obstacle before Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rashi and Targum Yonasan: Pharaoh spoke about Dasan and Aviram, who stayed in Egypt, and the Be'er Mayim Chaim brings a Chazal that the sea split a second time for them. To explain what changed, he contrasts the revealed world with the hidden world, alma d'iskasya, which was revealed at the sea. He illustrates the hidden world with shidduchim, which even a bas kol cannot grasp, and with Leah, whose tears tore her from Esav's root. The splitting on Shvi'i shel Pesach was only partial; the second one, in Acharon shel Pesach's haftarah, will reach even those left behind. He reconciles the Ibn Ezra and Ramban on the Shirah, brings the Rama MiFano that Eliyahu's two bulls were Dasan and Aviram, and concludes that today's machlokes is the Satan's work on the erev Shabbos before Moshiach, from which every Jew must run.

en: Dasan and Aviram stayed in Egypt, and according to a Chazal brought by the Be'er Mayim Chaim the sea split a second time for them.
At the splitting of the sea, on Shvi'i shel Pesach, the hidden world (alma d'iskasya) was revealed, as the Baal HaTanya says in Torah Ohr.
Acharon shel Pesach's haftarah speaks of a second, greater splitting of the sea in the days of Moshiach, which will be a path even for those who were left behind.
Every Jew, even the worst, has a hidden point of love for Hashem that can never be ruined, and it is revealed on the last days of Pesach.
Machlokes tears a Jew away from Hashem's oneness, and the Mashgiach says that whoever fears Heaven must resolve to have no part in any machlokes.
The machlokes of today comes because it is the erev Shabbos before Moshiach, when the Satan works to keep the light of Shabbos and peace from entering.

title.en: Dasan and Aviram stayed in Egypt

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the reading of Shvi'i shel Pesach: Rashi and Targum Yonasan explain that Pharaoh spoke of those who stayed in Egypt, Dasan and Aviram, and the Be'er Mayim Chaim brings a Chazal that the sea split a second time for them. He asks what changed in them at the sea, and also raises the dispute of the Ibn Ezra and the Ramban whether 'ki va sus Paroh' is part of the Shirah.

title.en: The bas kol and the hidden world

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Megillah that when Yonasan ben Uziel translated the Prophets a bas kol asked who revealed its secrets, and he had to stand up and say it was he; he asks why the bas kol did not know. He introduces the revealed and hidden worlds, and the Baal HaTanya's teaching that at the splitting of the sea the hidden was uncovered, as the covering sea turned into dry land.

title.en: Shidduchim come from the hidden world

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Tzemach Tzedek that the root of a shidduch is so high it cannot descend into the physical world until a shadchan's untruth brings it down, and tells how the Divrei Chaim paid every shadchan even when the match did not go through. He explains that a bas kol is lower than prophecy and unclear, so it cannot grasp a hidden zivug and announces wrong matches until the right one; this is why it did not know who Yonasan ben Uziel was.

title.en: Leah's tears and Esav's hidden spark

summary.en: From the Heichal HaBrachah the Mashgiach explains that Esav, 'admoni' like David, carried a high spark of holiness from the hidden world. Leah too is of the hidden world while Rachel is of the revealed, so Leah was fit for Esav; with her tears she tore herself from Esav's root into Yaakov's and changed her mazal, a revelation of the hidden world like the splitting of the sea.

title.en: The second splitting of the sea

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Shvi'i shel Pesach, when the sea split, with Acharon shel Pesach, whose haftarah from Yeshayahu speaks of a second splitting still hidden, 'yosif Hashem shenis yado'. Then high souls now buried deep in the mud will have their tikkun; the sea did not want to split the first time because the Jews were not yet ready, but in the future all Jews will pass through, those not ready tearing themselves from their root of evil with tears.

title.en: Yosef's coffin and the sea's refusal

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Jews kept their holiness in Egypt in Yosef's merit, apart from Shlomis bas Divri, and that the sea split when it saw Yosef's coffin, since Yosef had split his own 'sea', the yetzer hara. He asks why Hashem then had to rebuke the sea, and answers with the Be'er Mayim Chaim's Chazal: the rebuke was for the second splitting, for Dasan and Aviram, who had no share in Yosef's holiness.

title.en: Do Dasan and Aviram have a share in Olam Haba?

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Mishnah in Sanhedrin and the Braisa of the 'doreshei reshumos' who hold that even those listed have a share, proven from 'morid Sheol vaya'al'. The Ohr HaChaim says that even Korach's company has a share, but not Dasan and Aviram, who have no tikkun; the Tiferes Shlomo protests that every Jew will reach his tikkun and shows that 'morid Sheol vaya'al' equals Dasan and Aviram in gematria.

title.en: A path for those who were left behind

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Acharon shel Pesach's haftarah, 'vehaysa mesilah lish'ar amo', promises a path for those who stayed in Egypt. The exodus came before its time, from the forty-nine gates of impurity, but when Moshiach comes, through the power of the Torah, even those in the fiftieth gate will come out, as hinted in the Haggadah's answer to the rasha. He shows that Dasan and Aviram's whole career was machlokes, from 'nitzim' to 'nitzavim'.

title.en: The first splitting was only a sign

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that the haftarah of Acharon shel Pesach hints at Dasan and Aviram, and brings the Midrash that at the sea the Jews did not say 'Hashem melech', because the exodus came early and the exile had to complete it. With the Ramban's rule that the events of the fathers are a sign for the children, he concludes that the splitting on Shvi'i shel Pesach is a sign of the true one still to come, when even the worst Jew will reach his tikkun.

title.en: Machlokes, and the Shirah of Dasan and Aviram

summary.en: The Mashgiach says there is no damage like machlokes, which is the world of separation of the sitra achra, opposed to Hashem's oneness; Yerushalayim was destroyed because of it, and Dasan and Aviram were souls of separation. He then answers the opening question: the second 'uvnei Yisrael halchu bayabasha' refers to Dasan and Aviram crossing after the miracle ended, so the Ibn Ezra is right that it is part of a Shirah and the Ramban is right that it is not part of the Shirah of all Israel.

title.en: Eliyahu's two bulls and the tikkun at Ne'ilah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Rama MiFano that the two bulls Eliyahu brought on Har HaCarmel were Dasan and Aviram, and the Midrash that the bull meant for Ba'al refused until told that a kiddush Hashem would come through it too. He explains that achdus is the unity of Hashem, that Yom Kippur is the day of achdus, and that the two bulls reach their tikkun at Ne'ilah, when Jews cry out 'Hashem hu haElokim'.

title.en: The hidden point revealed at the sea

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Moshe mentions Dasan and Aviram and not Korach: Korach had a tikkun, while for Dasan and Aviram Hashem's wonder was the second splitting, and 'asah' means 'tikken'. He then answers the opening question: the plagues did not move them, but when the hidden world was revealed at the sea their hidden point awoke, they did teshuvah and ran to the sea. He calls to use Shvi'i and Acharon shel Pesach, when the hidden love in every Jew is revealed and even the last Jew can be raised.

title.en: Today's machlokes on the erev Shabbos of history

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that the machlokes among Jews today is the Satan's plan, since Moshiach will bring achdus, and that souls with sparks of Dasan and Aviram are among us. He says every Jew with fear of Heaven must resolve to have no part in any machlokes and to run from it, and that fighting between chassidus groups is a distortion of the Ba'al Shem Tov's way. He brings the Gemara in Gittin of the two men whom the Satan set quarreling every erev Shabbos until Rabbi Meir made peace, and explains that today is the erev Shabbos before Moshiach.

title.en: Shalom is Hashem's name

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that 'ki tov' is missing on the second day of creation because machlokes was created then, and explains that shalom is the name of Hashem and of Yerushalayim and is the test of whether a thing is desired by Hashem. He closes with the Baal HaTanya that Shvi'i shel Pesach is the Shabbos of Pesach, calls to work for shalom, and blesses that all Jews merit it together.

catalogTitle: Spiritual Coins are Created by our Desire to Give שקלים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jew's heartfelt desire to give the half-shekel creates spiritual coins, because deep in every Jewish heart lies a point no sin can reach, and he shows this point in Yom Kippur, Purim and the haftarah of King Yehoash.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash that Moshe Rabbeinu comes each year at Parshas Shekalim to lift up the Jewish people. He brings the Rema MiPano's question: how does the angel Michael offer korbanos in the heavenly Beis HaMikdash, when korbanos must come from each year's new shekalim? The Pri Tzaddik answers with Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who filled a valley with gold coins by his word: a Jew's yearning to give, when he hears Parshas Shekalim, creates spiritual coins. The Mashgiach ties Shekalim to the tip of the yud and to the hidden point in the heart described by the Rambam, the inner Holy of Holies that surfaces on Yom Kippur and Purim. He then shows that Yehoash, who killed Zechariah, is the haftarah's hero of the shekalim, proving that no sin reaches that point. He closes with a Gemara about Rabbah bar bar Chanah: more is demanded of a person on a higher level.

en: According to the Pri Tzaddik, the yearning of each Jew to give the shekel, aroused when Parshas Shekalim is read, creates spiritual coins from which the heavenly korbanos are bought.
Through the Rambam's ruling on a coerced consent, the Mashgiach explains that every Jew, even a rasha, has a hidden point in his heart that wants to do Hashem's will.
Since man is a small world, every Jew has an inner Holy of Holies, which comes into contact on Yom Kippur and, even more, on Purim.

Yehoash, who sinned against the Holy of Holies by killing Zechariah on Yom Kippur, is the one who strengthened the mitzvah of the shekalim, showing that no sin reaches the point that Shekalim touches.
Yom Kippur and Purim both come through a lottery, which has no reason, because they come from the root point where tzaddik and rasha are the same.
From the Gemara of Rabbah bar bar Chanah the Mashgiach learns that for a person on a higher level, what is middas chassidus for others is the din.

title.en: Moshe's yearly lift and the heavenly korbanos

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash that Moshe Rabbeinu comes each year at Parshas Shekalim to lift up every Jew. He then brings the Rema MiPano: the angel Michael offers korbanos in the heavenly Beis HaMikdash, and since korbanos must be bought from each year's new shekalim, the question is where the money comes from.

title.en: The Pri Tzaddik: coins created by desire

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Pri Tzaddik's answer through the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who turned a valley into gold coins by his word. A Jew too has the power of speech, so when he hears Parshas Shekalim and yearns to give, spiritual coins are created, and from them the heavenly korbanos are brought.

title.en: The tip of the yud and the hidden will

summary.en: The Mashgiach links the four parshiyos to the four letters of Hashem's Name, with Shekalim as the yud and its tiny tip that is above the Name. He then brings the Rambam on a man forced until he says 'I want': deep in every Jew's heart is a hidden point that wants Hashem's will, even in a rasha.

title.en: The inner Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur and Purim

summary.en: Since man is a small world, every Jew has a Holy of Holies inside him, which he touches on Yom Kippur, and Purim is a Yom Kippur that goes even higher. The Mashgiach explains the Jews' rescue in the Purim story and the merit of the shekalim that preceded Haman's shekalim through this point, where all Jews are equal.

title.en: The haftarah: Yehoash and Zechariah

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the story behind the haftarah: Yehoash was hidden as an infant in the Holy of Holies from Asalyah and crowned at seven by Yehoyada. After Yehoyada's death Yehoash had Yehoyada's son Zechariah, a kohen and navi, killed in the Beis HaMikdash on Yom Kippur.

title.en: World, year and soul: why Yehoash fits Shekalim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the world was made in three matching dimensions, place, time and soul, each with a Holy of Holies, so killing Zechariah on Yom Kippur near the Kodesh HaKodashim violated all three. Yet Yehoash is the one who strengthened the mitzvah of the shekalim, and the Mashgiach says no one fits the haftarah better, because Shekalim shows a point in the heart, the tip of the yud, that no sin reaches.

title.en: Two lotteries: Yom Kippur and Purim

summary.en: Following the Tanya, the Mashgiach notes that both Yom Kippur and Purim come through a lottery. The two identical goats, Yaakov and Esav, are separated only by lot; the Chasam Sofer's round dance of the tzaddikim shows all are equally close to the center; and a lottery win has no reason, because it comes from the root point. He concludes that Yehoash proves no sin reaches that point.

title.en: On the sedra: more is asked of the great

summary.en: The Mashgiach adds a word on the sedra with the Gemara of Rabbah bar bar Chanah, whose workers broke his wine barrel, and asks why Rav called it the din. He explains that the higher a person's level, the more is required of him, and illustrates it with a story of a brilliant student of Rebbe Reb Bunim of Peshischa who mocked a Zohar.

catalogTitle: בימי ספירה צריכים לעשות תשובה על שורש העבירות - המדות (שייכות לפרשת קדושים)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the days of Sefirah, as the beginning and root of the year, are the time to do teshuvah on the root of sin, the middos, and that this is the meaning of 'kedoshim tihyu'.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with 'kedoshim tihyu' and contrasts Chanoch, who separated himself and became an angel, with Avraham, who went down to the people. He then asks why there are three seasons of teshuvah: Sefirah, Shovavim, and Elul-Tishrei. Using the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nissan, he explains Nissan as the birth and chesed of creation and Tishrei as its full growth and din. A long thread follows on the first se'ir of Rosh Chodesh Nissan at the dedication of the Mishkan, which was burned because that day had no lessening of the moon, and on Nadav and Avihu, who sensed the days of Moshiach. Then he turns to his main point: Nissan and Sefirah are the time to repair the roots, the middos, from which sins grow, while Tishrei is for deeds and Shovavim for removing stains. He reads 'kedoshim tihyu' with the Ramban as sanctifying what is permitted, and urges everyone, by his own measure, to grow with nature during the remaining weeks.

en: The days of Sefirah are a season of teshuvah, one of three in the year together with Shovavim and Elul-Tishrei.
Nissan is the beginning and birth of creation, ruled by chesed; Tishrei is creation fully grown, ruled by din, matching the views of Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Eliezer.
The first se'ir of Rosh Chodesh, at the dedication of the Mishkan, was not eaten because on that day the moon was not diminished, and this is the best sign for all generations.
Every sin grows from a bad midda; whoever repents only for the sin and not for the midda falls back into the same sin.
In Nissan and Sefirah one repairs the middos, the root; in Tishrei the deeds, the fruit; and in Shovavim one removes the stains left after teshuvah.
'Kedoshim tihyu' means, as the Ramban explains, to sanctify oneself in what is permitted and not be a glutton within the Torah's permission, and it was said to all of Klal Yisroel.

title.en: Kedoshim tihyu: Chanoch and Avraham

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with 'kedoshim tihyu' and contrasts Chanoch, who withdrew and became an angel, with Avraham, who went down to people; holiness must not contradict closeness to others, which is why the parsha was said in public. He then brings the Chasam Sofer that Nadav and Avihu were reincarnated in Pinchas, who is Eliyahu, as a repair for their strange fire.

title.en: Three seasons of teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the days of Sefirah are days of tikkun and teshuvah, and that there are three such seasons: Sefirah, Shovavim and Elul-Tishrei. He asks how they differ, and begins with Nissan as the head of the months, bringing the Maharal that a beginning lasts for its first quarter.

title.en: Nissan's growth and the burned se'ir

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Nissan, Iyar and Sivan as the season of birth and growth in nature and in Klal Yisroel. He then asks why the first se'ir of Rosh Chodesh, offered on the day the Mishkan was set up, was burned and not eaten, when a beginning should be a good sign, and raises the question of how Nadav and Avihu could rule before Moshe and enter after drinking wine.

title.en: Tishrei and Nissan: din and chesed

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nissan, and explains that both are true: Nissan is the birth of creation in chesed, Tishrei its maturity in din. Each Tanna follows his own approach, and according to Rabbi Eliezer the beginning of the world is hinted in Bereishis, while the true beginning of the world is from its middle, Eretz Yisroel.

title.en: The middle of the Torah and Rosh Chodesh

summary.en: According to Rabbi Yehoshua, the beginning of creation is hinted in the middle of the Torah, at the words 'darosh darash' about the se'ir of the chatas. The Mashgiach connects Bereishis and 'se'ir' to the six hundred thousand souls of Klal Yisroel, and explains that the se'ir of Rosh Chodesh is an atonement for the lessening of the moon, which is Klal Yisroel in galus.

title.en: The day the Mishkan was set up

summary.en: Rosh Chodesh Nissan is the root of all roots, and the day the Mishkan was set up was, as the Gemara in Megillah says, like the day of creation, a taste of the days of Moshiach. On that day the moon was whole and needed no atonement, so not eating the se'ir was the best possible sign, and this is why it is hinted in the middle of the Torah.

title.en: Nadav and Avihu sensed the days of Moshiach

summary.en: Nadav and Avihu became the soul of Eliyahu, the herald of the redemption, and are 'after death'. The Mashgiach describes the days of Moshiach, when, as Yirmiyahu says, no one will need to teach another, and explains that Nadav and Avihu felt this so strongly on that day that they lost themselves; their entering after drinking wine shows their greatness, not their smallness.

title.en: Wine, Eliyahu and kevius

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Berachos that whether one may make a meal of wine will be decided when Eliyahu comes, the Midrash about the first vineyard planted, where wine turns a man into a sheep, a lion, a monkey and a pig, and the Gemara that wine's end is blood, explaining with gematria that a little wine holds Hashem's Name and too much leaves only 'dam'. Eliyahu is the holy side of the mazal of Ma'adim; Nadav and Avihu, sensing the time of Eliyahu when wine can no longer harm, entered after drinking.

title.en: Fifty-one days and Pesach Sheni

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that the Sefirah period, like Elul-Tishrei, has fifty-one days, hinted in the two 'na' of 'Ana Hashem' in Hallel, and that its thirtieth day, Pesach Sheni, parallels Rosh Hashanah as a day of tikkun. Mishael and Eltzafan, who became impure from Nadav and Avihu, merited the parsha of Pesach Sheni, showing that impurity of death can be repaired.

title.en: The middos are the root of sin

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Sefirah is the time to repair the middos, bringing Rabbi Chaim Vital that the middos are the root of all mitzvos and worse than sins, and the Be'er Mayim Chaim. He shows how lashon hara grows from arrogance, machlokes from the need to win, as with Yeravam ben Nevat, and eating forbidden food from desire, and says that people repeat sins because they did teshuvah on the sin and not on the midda.

title.en: Using each midda for good

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the middos: chesed through tzedakah, favors and learning with others; gevurah against the yetzer hara, even in permitted things; tiferes in knowing one's own great worth, so that every mitzvah, like counting the Omer, is precious; netzach in fighting for Yiddishkeit and not to defeat another; and hod in bowing down and praising Hashem.

title.en: Root, fruit and stains

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers his opening question: Nissan, when everything sprouts, is for repairing the root, the middos; Tishrei, the time of harvest, is for teshuvah on deeds; and Shovavim is a 'laundry season' for removing the stains that remain after teshuvah, as Rabbeinu Yonah writes. He adds that through Nadav and Avihu's self-sacrifice Aharon merited entering the Kodesh HaKodashim on Yom Kippur.

title.en: The Rambam's Sefer Kedushah in the Sefirah parshiyos

summary.en: Acharei-Kedoshim falls in the middle of Sefirah, the week of netzach, the axis around which Sefirah turns. The Mashgiach shows that almost all the halachos of the Rambam's Sefer Kedushah and Sefer Taharah are found in the parshiyos read during Sefirah, and even the few exceptions connect to Shavuos or are hinted there.

title.en: The Ramban on kedoshim tihyu

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the Ramban that 'kedoshim tihyu' warns against being a glutton within the Torah's permission and commands sanctifying oneself in what is permitted, which is the repair of middos rather than deeds. He brings Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim 231, that all one does should be for Hashem, and says that our weak generation cannot demand great things of itself.

title.en: Kedoshim for everyone; grow with nature

summary.en: Since the parsha was said to the whole congregation, the Mashgiach says 'kedoshim tihyu' is for everyone, each by his own measure and with sense: stopping now and then from an extra treat, eating enough to serve Hashem with joy, and not fooling oneself. He closes by urging the listeners to use the remaining weeks of Sefirah, to look at nature growing each day and to grow with it until Shavuos.

catalogTitle: תיקון המדות הנוגע למעשה.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the weeks of Sefirah are the time to become a true 'adam' through good middos, above all by never shaming another person, since Torah can only be received by people of good character.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by explaining that the seven weeks of Sefirah are for refining the seven middos, which is why Pirkei Avos is learned then; Rabbi Chaim Vital teaches that middos are not written in the Torah because they are the prerequisite for receiving it. Over Sefirah a person must become an 'adam', and in the generation before Moshiach, marked by chutzpah, this work is urgent. He then brings a chain of examples from Sefer Bereishis and Chazal: Beis Hillel's humility, Rachel handing the simanim to Leah, Tamar ready to be burned rather than shame Yehuda, Yosef risking his life not to shame his brothers, the chol bird, and Shaul with his servant. He warns against frumkeit that shames others, contrasts Tamar with Potiphar's wife, and stresses kavod habriyos, ahavas Yisrael and respect for another's opinion. He closes with the Kohen Gadol who must tend to a meis mitzvah even on Yom Kippur.

en: The seven weeks of Sefirah are given for perfecting the seven middos, which are the entrance requirement for receiving the Torah on Shavuos.
In the era before Moshiach, whose main sign is chutzpah, one must work especially hard to become a mentsch.
Rachel, Tamar and Yosef merited the geulah, the kingship of David and great blessings because they refused to shame another person.
Frumkeit that is used to shame and attack others is, according to the Mashgiach, a bad middah; one must be ehrlich, and rebuke only gently and with love.
The Torah is particular about kavod habriyos, which can even override the Kohen Gadol's Yom Kippur service.
Love of a fellow Jew is bound together with love of Hashem and love of Torah.
What a person learns shapes his middos: Torah study in a given area brings care in that area.

title.en: Sefirah as the time for perfecting middos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the seven weeks of counting are for refining the seven middos, character traits rather than piety, and that this is why Pirkei Avos is learned between Pesach and Shavuos. He brings Rabbi Chaim Vital that middos are hardly written in the Torah because they are the entrance requirement for receiving it.

title.en: Becoming an 'adam' by Shavuos

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the siddur of the Yaavetz that the blessing of Sefiras HaOmer hints to the name of Hashem whose spelled-out letters equal 'adam', and contrasts the barley Omer, animal food, with the human food brought on Shavuos. He then brings the Gemara at the end of Sotah that chutzpah marks the time before Moshiach and the Arizal's words about his generation.

title.en: Simple middos and Beis Hillel's humility

summary.en: The Mashgiach announces that in the coming weeks he will speak about simple middos, not sharp chiddushim, since simplicity is the beauty of a Jew. He brings the Gemara that Beis Hillel merited that the halacha follows them because they were gentle and humble, quoting Beis Shammai's view first.

title.en: Rachel's simanim and the redemption

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells how Rachel gave Leah the signs she had arranged with Yaakov so that her sister would not be shamed, and how she never revealed it. Through the Midrash on 'Rachel weeps for her children' he shows that the redemption comes in her merit, and explains that her test was one of middos, not of tefillah or mitzvos.

title.en: Tamar, and frumkeit that shames

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Tamar was ready to be burned rather than publicly shame Yehuda, and how she merited the kingship of David; the Gemara learns from her that one should rather be thrown into a fire than shame another. He applies this to people who shame others in the name of frumkeit, bringing the sayings of the Belzer Rav and the Ropshitzer, and says rebuke must be private and with love.

title.en: Yosef's danger rather than shaming his brothers

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that Yosef put himself in mortal danger by sending everyone out before revealing himself, so as not to shame his brothers before the Egyptians, and that his greatness came from these middos. He adds that Sefer Bereishis has almost no mitzvos and teaches middos, and brings the Bnei Yissaschar that this is why Avos is learned before Matan Torah.

title.en: Covering for sinners at war; the chol bird

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Torah sends home newlyweds and others from war so that one who is afraid because of his sins will not be recognized and shamed. He then tells the Gemara of the chol bird that did not ask Noach for food so as not to burden him, and was blessed never to die.

title.en: Middos as the foundation; Yosef avoids his father

summary.en: The Mashgiach says good middos are the foundation of yiras Shamayim, of chassidus and of Torah, and that a chassid without them is a false chassid. He brings from the Rishonim that Yosef avoided being alone with Yaakov for seventeen years so that he would not have to tell how his brothers sold him.

title.en: Tamar and Potiphar's wife: both for Heaven's sake

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why, if both Tamar and Potiphar's wife acted for Heaven's sake, as Rashi says, one is praised and the other shamed forever. He answers that Tamar would not shame Yehuda, while Potiphar's wife threw Yosef into prison; he applies it to zealotry that shames people, and brings the Divrei Chaim's proof that burying a rasha is no mitzvah.

title.en: Shaul and his servant; kavod habriyos in Shema

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows how Shaul, searching for the lost donkeys, spoke of his father worrying about 'us', putting his servant on a par with himself, and was told that this is why he would become king. He then brings the Mishnah that one may interrupt Kriyas Shema to greet out of respect, though one may not even gesture, showing how the Torah values kavod habriyos.

title.en: Parshas Kedoshim and the three loves

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's students rejoiced when Parshas Kedoshim came, since it holds 'love your fellow as yourself', Rabbi Akiva's great principle. He connects love of a fellow Jew to love of Hashem, brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's three loves, and says one should accept this mitzvah before davening so the tefillah is accepted.

title.en: The poor man's offering and a bochur's chiddush

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that only by the poor man's mincha does the Torah say 'nefesh', and that the poor man's bird is burned with its feathers despite the bad smell, yet it is a pleasing aroma to Hashem; he brings the Rambam that the incense was to counter the smell of the offerings. He applies this to a bochur who offers a weak chiddush to a great lamdan, who should accept it warmly.

title.en: Different faces, different opinions

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that just as people's faces differ so do their opinions, and explains that each person has a different neshamah and root, as Hillel came from chessed and Shammai from gevurah, so their faces and rulings differed. He concludes that one may prefer his own view but may never say another's view is nothing.

title.en: Rav Aharon Kotler: learning shapes middos

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rav Aharon Kotler's observation that Litvishe Jews are more careful in bein adam lachaveiro and chassidim in bein adam laMakom, because chassidim learn mostly Seder Moed and Brachos while Litvishe yeshivos learn the Bava's, and Torah instills what one learns. He adds the tzaddikim's teaching to learn a Yom Tov's masechta before the Yom Tov.

title.en: The Kohen Gadol and kavod habriyos

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a member of the Gerer family who delayed breaking his fast after Yom Kippur to finish Masechta Yoma, then brings the case of a Kohen Gadol on Erev Yom Kippur who finds a meis mitzvah and must become tamei even at the cost of the avodah, because kavod habriyos is great. He closes that Sefirah is the time to reflect on how to improve in bein adam lachaveiro, ahavas Yisrael and kavod habriyos.

catalogTitle: The Lesson of the מגילה: Find 'ה Peeking Through the Cracks of Your life. Explanation of פורים קטן

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that Purim and its Megillah train a Jew to find Hashem hidden behind nature, rulers and events, peeking out through the cracks, and explains Purim Katan of a leap year.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the greatness of Purim, compared with Yom Kippur, and explains Purim Katan: in a leap year the moon has fallen far behind the sun, so in the first Adar we are too weak to keep Purim, and Hashem has the Megillah read in heaven; the second reading, in the second Adar, accomplishes more. He then explains Amalek through three readings of 'karcha': cooling a Jew's fervor, making him impure, and teaching that everything is chance. This is the 'double hiding' of 'haster astir', which is why Hashem's name seems absent from the Megillah and hides in the word 'hamelech', whose gematria equals the incomplete 'kes Kah'. Through the Bnei Yissaschar's parable he shows that a miracle inside nature is greater still. The Megillah trains the eye to find Hashem through the cracks, in history, in the news and behind every costume. He closes with Adar as the month of laughter at the world, Yaakov's complaint, Mordechai, and David's response to Shimi.

en: In a leap year the first Adar is too far from the 'sun' of Hashem for us to keep Purim, so Hashem has the Megillah read in heaven, and the second reading in the second Adar accomplishes more.
Amalek 'cooled off' the Jews; life always pulses up and down, and the war against Amalek is to hold on through the cold periods until Hashem warms a person again.
Amalek and Haman stand for the belief that everything is chance ('mikreh'), which is the double concealment of 'haster astir' that marks the Megillah and the time before Moshiach.
Hashem's name is hidden in the Megillah in the word 'hamelech', because His name and throne are incomplete ('kes Kah') while Amalek exists.
Adar is the season of miracles cloaked in nature, and reading the Megillah is an exercise in finding Hashem behind that cloak.
After Purim one should be able to read the news and all of history between the lines and see Hashem directing everything; the whole world is a Megillah.
Nothing happens without Hashem, so one may not blame a person for what happens to him, as seen from Yaakov's complaint and from David's response to Shimi.

title.en: The greatness of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach introduces Purim Katan this Shabbos and says Purim is greater than any Yom Tov: Yom Kippur is only 'like Purim', and in the future Yom Kippur will rise to Purim's level. Purim is 'masked', different from how it appears, like a child in costume.

title.en: Purim Katan and the second reading

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Megillah says 'hasheinis' in the feminine if it refers to the second month, and explains with the moon falling behind the sun: in the first Adar we are too weak to keep Purim, so Hashem has the Megillah read in heaven, as Michael offers on the altar above, and the second reading is greater.

title.en: Amalek cools off: the pulse of life

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Amalek represents the Satan and that 'asher karcha' means he cooled the Jews off. All life pulses up and down like a heartbeat or a pause in music, and the war against Amalek is to hold on through the cold until Hashem sends warmth again.

title.en: Karcha as impurity and as chance

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings two more readings of 'karcha': Amalek made the Jews impure, and Amalek teaches that things happen by chance ('mikreh'), denying Hashem's individual providence. He brings the Midrash calling Haman 'son of Korcha' and notes that Amalek equals 'safek', doubt, in gematria.

title.en: Haster astir: the double hiding

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Esther is hinted in 'haster astir' and the Ba'al Shem Tov's parable of a father who hides from his child, and then hides that he is hiding. This double concealment was the setting of the Megillah and, he says, is the state of most of Klal Yisrael before Moshiach, caused by Haman's philosophy of chance.

title.en: Hashem's name hidden in 'hamelech'

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Hashem's name is absent from the Megillah alone among the 24 books, because its setting is hester panim, and brings the Midrash on 'evel gadol', a mourning that grew as the decreed day approached. Yet, per the Midrash, every 'hamelech' in the Megillah refers to Hashem.

title.en: Kes Kah, the puppet king and the gematria of hamelech

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi on 'ki yad al kes Kah': Hashem's name and throne are incomplete until Amalek is erased, so His rule is concealed and we credit events to rulers. Achashverosh was a marionette moved by strings from above; 'hamelech' equals 'kes Kah' and Haman in gematria (95), and 'machi Amalek' equals 'kisei Havayah'.

title.en: Hidden miracles every day

summary.en: The Mashgiach says there are no open miracles in the Megillah, unlike Nisan, yet every person has hidden miracles daily, as said in Modim; the body is far more complex than a car and keeps working. In Adar the same miracles are cloaked in nature, and the Megillah story could have been reported in the newspapers.

title.en: The Bnei Yissaschar's parable: a miracle in nature

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Bnei Yissaschar's parable of a dying patient for whom the one doctor and the one medicine arrive just in time, showing that someone directs events without breaking nature, which is an even greater miracle. Adar is the season of such natural miracles, and 'Megillas Esther' means revealing the hidden.

title.en: Peeking through the cracks

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares reading the Megillah to a surgeon reading an x-ray and brings 'mashgiach min hachalonos, metzitz min hacharakim': Hashem watches through the cracks. He retracts his earlier statement: Hashem's name is in the Megillah, hidden in the initial and final letters of key phrases, as in 'yavo hamelech v'Haman hayom'.

title.en: The whole world is a Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that after Purim one should read the newspaper between the lines and see Hashem behind the world's leaders, and points to Eretz Yisrael always being in the headlines. The whole world is a Megillah to be revealed, and the Purim costumes teach to look beneath every disguise.

title.en: Adar, the month of laughter

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Sefer Yetzirah, which assigns each month an organ and activity: Adar's is laughter. The plague of locusts fell in Adar, where Hashem says He 'made sport' of Egypt. In Adar one laughs at the passing material world, as the Kotzker said the whole world is not worth a sigh, because Hashem directs everything.

title.en: Yaakov's complaint and Mordechai the 'troublemaker'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Yaakov once forgot himself and blamed his sons, while Hashem was making Yosef king. He then retells the nine years of the Megillah: Mordechai opposed going to Achashverosh's feast and refused to bow to Haman, and was blamed as a troublemaker, but in the end it was clear he was right all along.

title.en: David, Shimi and the lesson of the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that people blamed David for not killing Shimi, Mordechai's ancestor; in truth, because David saw that Hashem told Shimi to curse, Mordechai was born to teach hashgachah pratis and write the Megillah. He concludes that the same Achashverosh brought mourning and joy: all are puppets, and nothing happens without Hashem.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the 49 days of sefirah as a climb out of the 49 gates of impurity, mirrored in the desert journeys, in Ana Bekoach, in Lamenatzeach and in the 49 dafim of Masechta Sotah, whose closing mishnah on the footsteps of Moshiach he finds fulfilled in our own days.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the exodus: on the night of the Seder Hashem took the Jews out of the 49 gates of impurity as a free gift, and from the second day of Pesach they must earn it themselves, counting 49 days and refining the seven middos to reach the fiftieth day of Matan Torah. What each Jew does in sefirah, the whole people does in the desert and in galus: Parshas Masei lists 42 journeys, and with the seven they went back, as Rashi brings, there are 49. The same pattern of 42 plus seven appears in the 42-letter Name in Ana Bekoach and in Lamenatzeach. He then explains the custom of learning a daf of Sotah each day: the Jews were tested like a sotah, as the barley omer shows. The masechta ends with the mishnah on the footsteps of Moshiach, and he shows its signs today: chutzpah, rising prices, kingdoms turning to heresy, schools corrupted, the Galil in ruins, and the conclusion to rely only on our Father in Heaven.

en: On the Seder night the Jews were taken out of the 49 gates of impurity as a gift; from the second day of Pesach they must leave them by their own work, one gate each day of sefirah.
The 49 days of sefirah, the 49 journeys in the desert and the long galus are one path of 49 levels leading to the fiftieth: Matan Torah, Eretz Yisroel, the geulah.
The count of 49 is built as 42 plus seven: 42 journeys and seven retraced, 42 letters of the Name in Ana Bekoach and the line repeated at the end of each week.
Masechta Sotah, with its 49 dafim, belongs to sefirah: the Jews were tested like a sotah, which is why the omer, like the sotah's offering, is of barley, while on Shavuos the two loaves are of wheat.

The last daf of Sotah, reached on erev Shavuos, corresponds to malchus shebemalchus, the lowest level, and its mishnah describes the footsteps of Moshiach, the period the Mashgiach says we are in now.

The Mashgiach goes through the signs of the mishnah, chutzpah, high prices, kingdoms turning to heresy, places of study turned to immorality, the Galil destroyed and people wandering from city to city, and shows each one in the world of today.

title.en: From a free gift to forty-nine days of work

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that on the Seder night Hashem took the Jews out of the 49 gates of impurity in one moment as a gift, and from the second day of Pesach they must leave them by their own work. Each day of sefirah a Jew refines one of the seven times seven middos, to reach the fiftieth day of Matan Torah and the root of the Avos.

title.en: Forty-nine journeys in the desert and in galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach says what each Jew goes through in sefirah, the whole people goes through on a larger scale: the 49 journeys in the desert, each a place of impurity, and the long galus, where each period passes one journey until the geulah. He shows from Parshas Masei and Rashi that the 42 listed journeys are 49 with the seven the Jews went back.

title.en: Ana Bekoach and Lamenatzeach: 42 plus seven

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the 42-letter Name and the tefillah of Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah built on it, and asks how its 42 letters fit the 49 days; the answer is that at the end of each week the whole line is said again. He shows the same count of 49 in Lamenatzeach and its middle passuk, and ties it all to the 49 stations of the desert, sefirah and galus.

title.en: A daf of Sotah each day of sefirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the custom of learning a daf of Masechta Sotah each day of sefirah, finishing on erev Shavuos, and gives the simple reason, to keep track of the count. He then explains the deeper link: the Jews were tested like a sotah, which is why the omer is of barley like the sotah's offering, and each daf brings them a day closer to Har Sinai.

title.en: The last daf: chutzpah and rising prices

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the last daf of Sotah, learned on erev Shavuos, is malchus shebemalchus and opens with the footsteps of Moshiach, which the Chofetz Chaim already saw in his time. He illustrates the chutzpah of today from his own memories of respect for teachers, then explains the law of supply and demand to show how the mishnah's rising prices defy it.

title.en: The kingdom turns to heresy

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that minus means believing in nothing, and that even an idolater restrained himself out of belief; he tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov jumped off a wagon whose driver did not cross himself before a priest. He contrasts the old kings and early America with today's unbelief, then shows how the school buildings of Williamsburg illustrate the house of study turned to immorality.

title.en: The Galil, the wanderers, and our Father in Heaven

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows the Galil emptied by rockets and the people of Eretz Yisroel going from city to city collecting to marry off their children, and concludes that everything in the mishnah is being fulfilled. Its last words teach that one can rely only on our Father in Heaven, and he calls on ehrliche Yidden to be the exceptions of the generation.

catalogTitle: ביאור הזוהר “בשבועות יפקון מגלותא;“ הלכות טהרה וקדושה בפרשיות הספירה; לימוד פרקי אבות - דרך ארץ קדמה לתורה

oneLiner.en: Starting from the tumah of a yoledes in parshas Tazria, the Mashgiach shows how the days of Sefirah are counted days of purifying and refining one's midos, so as to be let into Yerushalayim and Har Sinai on Shavuos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the parsha of the yoledes and asks why a mother who brought a Jewish child into the world becomes tamei. Following the Ohr HaChaim's explanation of why a Jewish corpse defiles in an ohel, he explains that the holiness she carried has emptied out, and asks why a boy then brings less tumah than a girl. The answer is the bris: Eliyahu, who never ate from the Etz HaDaas, comes, and the tumah is cut short; this is why the verse of milah interrupts the passage. From there he turns to Sefirah as preparation for the fiftieth day, explains the Zohar that the redemption will come 'on Shavuos', and shows that the Sefirah parshiyos hold Rambam's Sefer Taharah and Sefer Kedushah. The counted days are too precious to be nullified. He closes with Pirkei Avos and derech eretz before Torah, Rabbi Akiva's students, and lashon hara, which drives a person out of Yerushalayim.

en: A yoledes becomes tamei because the great holiness she carried, a child learning the whole Torah with an angel, has emptied out of her.
At a bris, Eliyahu HaNavi comes and the tumah is cut short, which is why the verse of milah on the eighth day interrupts the laws of the yoledes.
The days of Sefirah prepare for the fiftieth day, a day of yovel, return and redemption; this is how the Mashgiach reads the Zohar that the redemption will come on Shavuos.
The parshiyos read during Sefirah contain nearly all of Rambam's Sefer Taharah and Sefer Kedushah, because these are the weeks of becoming pure and holy.
The days of Sefirah are counted, a davar shebeminyan, and like any counted thing they are too precious ever to be nullified.
Good midos are a prerequisite for receiving the Torah, so in the weeks before Shavuos one learns Pirkei Avos and refines one's midos.
Lashon hara drove the Jews out of Yerushalayim, and today it keeps a person from reaching Yerushalayim in his tefillah and from the light of a blatt Gemara.

title.en: Why does a yoledes become tamei?

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the opening verses of Tazria and asks why a mother who brought a life into the world, and carried a child learning Torah with an angel, should become tamei. He also asks why the verse of milah on the eighth day appears in the middle of the laws of tumah.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim: holiness that has emptied out

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ohr HaChaim's parable of flies drawn to an emptied barrel of honey to explain why a Jewish corpse defiles in an ohel and a gentile's does not, and applies it to the yoledes. He then asks why a boy, whose holiness is greater, brings only seven days of tumah and a girl fourteen.

title.en: Closeness of family between souls

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that close family ties reflect a closeness between souls and create halachos, as with aveilus. He asks why the mother may wear Shabbos clothes at a bris on Tisha B'Av though she has no obligation in the milah, and answers that her closeness to the child brings her into its simcha.

title.en: Eliyahu at the bris cuts off tumah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Eliyahu never ate from the Etz HaDaas, so at a bris, a moment of the days of Moshiach, tumah is nullified. This answers why a boy brings less tumah and why the verse of milah interrupts the passage, and through the rule of lo plug it applies even when the milah is delayed.

title.en: The Zohar: redemption on Shavuos

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the days of Sefirah as preparation for the fiftieth day, the day of yovel. He brings the Zohar that the redemption will come on Shavuos, contrasts it with the Gemara's Nissan or Tishrei, and explains it through the distinction between 'b'itah' and 'achishena': Shavuos is a time especially suited for Moshiach.

title.en: Shavuos as the eighth day; Rambam's two books

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shavuos, the fiftieth day and the first of the eighth week, is like the eighth day on which a tamei person may immerse, and that the day itself is a mikveh. He then explains the name Yad HaChazakah and shows that two of its fourteen books, Sefer Taharah and Sefer Kedushah, are found in the Sefirah parshiyos.

title.en: Counted days of taharah and kedushah

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the parshiyos from Shemini to Emor and shows the laws of tumah and taharah and of kedushah in each. He brings the Gerrer Rebbe that these are counted days, and explains through the halacha of davar shebeminyan that counted days are too precious to be nullified; in them a person can be entirely renewed.

title.en: Iyar, the month of ziv

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Iyar is called the month of ziv: the fields blossom then because above, too, there is a radiance, the month the Beis HaMikdash was completed. A person is like a tree of the field, and through the mitzvah of Sefirah, which fills all of Iyar, he should blossom by purifying his seven midos.

title.en: Pirkei Avos: derech eretz before Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the original custom is to learn Pirkei Avos between Pesach and Shavuos because it deals with refining midos, derech eretz that precedes Torah. He brings Rabbi Chaim Vital that the Torah hardly speaks of midos because they are a prerequisite for learning it, and explains that Rabbi Akiva's students died in these weeks because midos are demanded more then.

title.en: Lashon hara and exile from Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tzaraas comes from lashon hara and that the metzora is sent out of all of Yerushalayim, and that the whole galus, symbolized by Kamtza and bar Kamtza, came from sins between man and his fellow. Today such a person is barred from Yerushalayim in his Shemoneh Esrei and from the light of the Gemara; he closes that Sefirah must be counted with the aim of refining one's midos.

catalogTitle: לימוד מס' סוטה - בירור טהרת כלל ישראל. דף מ"ט כנגד זמננו עקבתא דמשיחא

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that learning Maseches Sotah during Sefirah testifies to the purity of Klal Yisrael, and that its last daf, with the baraisa of the heels of Moshiach, corresponds to our generation, whose task is emunah, strengthened above all through heartfelt tefillah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the custom of learning a daf of Sotah each day of Sefirah. Beyond keeping count, he explains, both the sotah's offering and the Omer are of barley, and both come to show that Klal Yisrael kept its sanctity. He then describes Klal Yisrael across the generations as the full form of Adam HaRishon: the generation of the desert was the head, which learned Torah, David HaMelech's era the heart, which sang and davened, and our generation the heel, the darkest and lowest, the forty-ninth level before the fiftieth. The forty-ninth daf of Sotah, with the baraisa of the heels of Moshiach, is our generation, and what remains is to rely on our Father in Heaven, that is, emunah. Emunah is cleansed through Torah for the head and tefillah for the heart. He closes with the place of tefillah, including a child's kvitel at the Kosel, as the work of these times.

en: Sotah is learned during Sefirah because the sotah's offering and the Omer are both barley, and both come to clarify the sanctity of Klal Yisrael.
The generations of Klal Yisrael together form the full stature of Adam HaRishon, from the head down to the heel.
Our generation is the heel of Moshiach, the forty-ninth and lowest level, which will suddenly be overturned into the head of all generations.
The last daf of Sotah, 49b, with the baraisa ending that we can rely only on our Father in Heaven, corresponds to our generation; its task is emunah.
Emunah is purified by cleansing the head with Torah and the heart with tefillah, and a person needs both.
Tefillah is itself emunah, since one speaks to Hashem and asks of Him; even a prayer for small things expresses faith that He can give.

title.en: Why Sotah is learned during Sefirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the custom of learning one daf of Sotah's forty-nine each day of Sefirah, which keeps the count. The inner reason: the sotah's barley offering and the barley Omer both come to clarify the sanctity of Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Klal Yisrael as the form of Adam HaRishon

summary.en: From the Midrash that all souls hang on the limbs of Adam HaRishon, the Mashgiach explains that each Jew belongs to a limb: Torah scholars to the head, those whose avodah is tefillah to the heart, givers of tzedakah to the hands, and the lowest souls to the heel, which is always in darkness.

title.en: The generations from head to heel

summary.en: The Mashgiach lays the generations along the body: the generation of the desert was the head, David HaMelech the heart, and our generation the heel. Like Adar turning into Nisan, the forty-ninth and lowest level will suddenly be overturned into the head of all generations.

title.en: Daf 49b: our generation and emunah

summary.en: The last daf of Sotah holds the baraisa of the heels of Moshiach, which describes our generation and ends that we can rely only on our Father in Heaven. The Mashgiach explains that in a world full of heresy the task is emunah: Klal Yisrael began with Avraham's emunah and with Anochi at Sinai, and it ends with emunah.

title.en: The summit of Amanah and a child's emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that at the ingathering the Jews will stand on Mount Amanah and sing, meaning they will strengthen themselves in emunah. Every Jew, even a small child, has simple emunah, which can become sick and lose its appetite for holiness; he tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov as a melamed asked children whether they remembered standing at Sinai.

title.en: Cleansing the head with Torah, the heart with tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains how one works on emunah: the head is cleansed with Torah and the heart with tefillah. In the time before Moshiach the main thing is tefillah, yet bochurim must invest in Torah; learning without davening and davening without learning are each worthless, as a person cannot live without a brain or a heart.

title.en: Tefillah is emunah: the kvitel at the Kosel

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of pouring out the soul in tefillah, with tears, as David HaMelech and the authors of Yedid Nefesh and Shir HaShirim did, and says tefillah is the way toward Moshiach because it is emunah. He tells of a kvitel from the Kosel in which an Israeli boy asked Hashem for a dog and a bicycle, and explains that such a request too is emunah.

title.en: Tefillah stands at the height of the world

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that tefillah stands at the height of the world yet people treat it lightly, and urges investing in davening. He stresses David HaMelech's Pesukei d'Zimra as the root of tefillah, tied to Moshiach through the word sichah, and closes with asking Hashem for understanding and attachment rather than a bicycle.

catalogTitle: The Love of Hashem to Even the Lowest Jew

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach shows from Amalek, Haman and the silver hooks of the Mishkan that Hashem never forgets even the most distant Jew, and that Purim is the Yom Tov of the rejected.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach asks how Amalek dared attack Klal Yisrael under the Clouds of Glory, and answers that he attacked only those of Shevet Dan whom the clouds spat out for carrying an idol. Because Amalek struck these sinners, Hashem's war with Amalek lasts for all generations, which shows how He loves even a fallen Jew. Haman repeated the mistake: he saw the Jews' sins in Achashverosh's time and thought Hashem no longer cared for them. The Mashgiach then explains that the silver of the 1,775 shekels became the hooks of the pillars, which protrude outside the Mishkan and stand for the rejected Jews; Moshe forgot them, and the soul of Rabbi Akiva, the 'heel', reminded him. Haman paid no counterweight for these Jews, and his decree turned back on him. Purim is therefore the comfort of the simplest Jew. Adar, the end of the golus, and Adar Sheni outside the twelve combinations, call for teshuvah, and a ben Torah's teshuvah lifts all of Klal Yisrael.

en: Amalek could attack only the Jews of Shevet Dan whom the Clouds of Glory had rejected because of their idol, and Hashem's war with Amalek for all generations comes from his attacking these fallen Jews.
Haman made the same mistake as Amalek: seeing the Jews' sins in Achashverosh's time, he thought Hashem would no longer protect them.
The silver of the 1,775 shekels went to the hooks of the pillars, which protrude outside the Mishkan, and these represent Jews who seem rejected and forgotten.
Haman thought the rejected Jews needed no counterweight to their shekalim, but Hashem had not forgotten them, and the decree turned back on Haman and Amalek.
Purim is the comfort and hope of the simplest and most distant Jew, since it shows that no Jew is ever written off by Hashem.
Before Moshiach every Jew will do teshuvah; even a small teshuvah is a start, and Adar, the end of the golus, is a time for it.
Klal Yisrael is like one rope: when a ben Torah raises himself through teshuvah and Torah, the bottom of the rope rises as well.

title.en: Whom Amalek was able to attack

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how Amalek dared attack the Jews under the Clouds of Glory, and explains that he struck only those of Shevet Dan whom the clouds spat out for carrying the idol of Michah. Hashem's war with Amalek for all generations shows how much He loves even a Jew who has fallen.

title.en: Haman repeats Amalek's mistake

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the Jews of Haman's time were liable for bowing to the image and enjoying Achashverosh's feast, and explains that Haman, like his grandfather Amalek, thought this left them unprotected. He then describes the camp of Dan at the edge of the Machaneh, and how the Mishkan's camps parallel the Beis HaMikdash, the Azarah and Yerushalayim.

title.en: The hooks outside the Mishkan and Rabbi Akiva

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jew's half-shekel became the silver sockets of the Mishkan, but some silver went to the hooks that protrude outside the curtains, representing Jews who seem rejected and forgotten. Moshe Rabbeinu forgot what that silver was used for, and the soul of Rabbi Akiva, the 'heel' of Klal Yisrael and the head of Torah she'baal peh in golus, reminded him.

title.en: Haman's shekalim and the joy of the simple Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Haman offered his silver only against the Jews whose silver went to the sockets, thinking the rejected ones needed no counterweight; but Hashem remembered them, and the decree turned back on Haman so that Amalek's memory is erased. Therefore Purim is the Yom Tov of the simplest Jew, who feels at home on it.

title.en: Every Jew will do teshuvah before Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara and the Rambam that before Moshiach all Jews will do teshuvah, and if not, a ruler like Haman will force them to. He explains from Hashiveinu in Shemoneh Esrei that a small teshuvah is a first step, and describes today's 'drizzle' of teshuvah that will become a storm when Moshiach comes and the rejected are readmitted.

title.en: Adar Sheni and the ben Torah's teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Adar is the end of the golus and a month of teshuvah, and that Adar Sheni stands outside the twelve combinations of the Shem Havayah, like the Jews outside the camp, yet Purim is for them too. He closes with the Chofetz Chaim's words that one ben Torah's bittul Torah affects a distant Jew, and that Klal Yisrael is like one rope, so a ben Torah's teshuvah lifts everyone.

catalogTitle: תיקון המדות הנוגע למעשה - הוכחות מתנ"ך ומהלכה על חומר הענין

oneLiner.en: In the days of Sefirah the Mashgiach gathers proofs from Tanach, Chazal and halachah that one must guard the honor of every person and every creature, and never shame anyone.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the students of Rabbi Akiva, who died in the days of Sefirah because they did not treat one another with respect, and explains that good middos are the vessel for receiving the Torah, so these weeks are the time to work on them. He announces that in the coming weeks he will speak about middos between man and his fellow, and he even rebukes his own community for weak middos. He then brings a long chain of proofs: Avraham's hospitality, Beis Hillel, Rachel, Yosef, Tamar, the punishment of Yaakov for Esav's cry, Boaz and Manoach, the stones of the mizbe'ach, the Etz HaDa'as, the soldiers who return from war, and the bird offered with its feathers. He compares Tamar to the wife of Potiphar and explains that shaming someone is worse than taking one's own life, illustrated with stories of the Bluzhever Rebbe. He ends with practical cases: different opinions, curses, children, Purim jokes and correcting the Torah reader.

en: Good middos are the vessel for Torah, so the Sefirah days before Shavuos are the time to repair them, and the students of Rabbi Akiva were punished then for lacking respect for one another.
Every creature was made by Hashem with wisdom, so one must respect and have mercy even on animals, plants and stones.
Shaming another person in public is so grave that Tamar preferred to be burned rather than shame Yehudah, and the Mashgiach says it is worse than taking one's own life.
Tamar and the wife of Potiphar both acted for the sake of Heaven to bring Moshiach, and the difference between them was only good middos.
Just as faces differ, so do opinions, and one may not resent another person for thinking differently.
The Mashgiach applies kavod habriyos to daily life: encouraging a weak answer or a small gift, not cursing any Jew, not embarrassing children or making jokes at another's expense.
